item_7.notes:
[chunk 1/1] Key extractions from AMZN 10-K (FY2023, filed 2024-02-02):

1. ANTHROPIC INVESTMENT (CIRCULARITY): Amazon invested $1.25B in a convertible note in Anthropic in 2023, with a committed option for an additional $2.75B (up to $4B total). Anthropic is simultaneously a major AWS compute customer, creating a classic investor-is-also-customer circularity. Severity 3.

2. SERVER USEFUL-LIFE EXTENSION (COST OPACITY): Amazon extended the estimated useful life of servers effective January 1, 2024, reducing Q1 2024 depreciation by ~$900M. This is a material accounting policy change that flatters near-term earnings without changing underlying cash economics. Severity 3.

3. HIDDEN LEVERAGE — LEASE STACK: Long-term lease liabilities of $77.3B (Dec 31 2023) + long-term debt of $58.3B = ~$135B combined off-income-statement obligations. Finance lease principal repayments alone were $4.4B in 2023. Severity 3.

4. RIVIAN EQUITY VOLATILITY: Amazon holds a large equity stake in Rivian (marketable), which caused a $(12.7)B loss in 2022 and a $797M gain in 2023 — P&L swings of this magnitude from a single equity position represent meaningful earnings opacity. Severity 2.

5. CAPEX ROI GAP: $48.1B capex in 2023 with explicit management commitment to increase in 2024, primarily for AWS infrastructure. No matching contracted revenue disclosures in this section. Severity 2.

6. Finance leases: $642M equipment acquired under finance leases in 2023; $4.4B principal repayments on finance leases — treated as off-balance financing in free cash flow non-GAAP metrics, obscuring true capital intensity.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 3/3] Source section is Notes 9–10 plus segment data from AMZN 10-K filed 2024-02-02. Key observations:

1. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 3): The filing reports $276.7B combined PP&E net + operating leases as of Dec 31, 2023 ($196B U.S. + $80.7B non-U.S.). Operating leases are commingled with PP&E in the disclosure, obscuring true on-balance-sheet debt vs. off-balance-sheet obligations.

2. BUILD-TO-SUIT LEASES (severity 2): Peak $8.8B of build-to-suit lease arrangements added in 2021 (North America + International + AWS) has now tapered to ~$357M in 2023, suggesting the wave of off-balance-sheet construction risk has largely migrated onto the balance sheet — but the historical scale warrants monitoring.

3. TAX CONTINGENCIES — LTA (severity 2): Luxembourg denied tax basis of intangibles distributed to U.S. in 2021. Quantified exposure not yet determinable; cash outflow required upon assessment even while Amazon contests.

4. TAX CONTINGENCIES — ITA (severity 2): Indian tax authority asserting withholding on AWS cloud fees paid to U.S. entity. Described as "significant in the aggregate" with risk of additional expense on taxes already paid if adversely resolved.

5. AWS PROFIT CONCENTRATION (severity 1): AWS = 15.8% of 2023 revenue but ~66.8% of operating income ($24.6B of $36.9B). North America and International combined earned only $12.2B on $484B revenue. This segment concentration amplifies any AWS demand shock.

6. No investments, SPVs, or named AI lab relationships were disclosed in this specific filing section. Capex commitments and equity investments in AI labs (e.g., Anthropic) would appear in other sections (Note 6, commitments and contingencies) not included here.
